VolgoMetall Expands Smelting Capacity with $220 Million Investment in Central Russia

Russian metals producer VolgoMetall has announced a major expansion of its smelting operations, committing $220 million to boost capacity at its flagship plant in the Tula region. The project, which is scheduled for completion in late 2025, aims to increase annual steel output by 400,000 tonnes, strengthening the company’s presence in domestic and export markets.

The investment will fund the construction of a new electric arc furnace, a state-of-the-art rolling mill, and upgraded environmental controls. VolgoMetall said the expansion is designed to meet growing demand from the construction, engineering, and manufacturing sectors in Russia and neighboring countries.

“Our commitment to this project reflects our confidence in the resilience of the Russian metals market and our desire to support key industries with reliable supply,” said Alexei Yermakov, VolgoMetall’s general director. “We expect the new facilities to be among the most efficient and environmentally responsible in the region.”

The company estimates that the expansion will create up to 350 new jobs during the construction phase and 180 permanent positions once operations begin. Local officials have welcomed the announcement, citing the positive impact on the regional economy and supply chain.

“VolgoMetall’s investment is a strong vote of confidence in the Tula region’s industrial base and workforce,” said Andrei Sokolov, deputy governor for economic development. “The project will support local suppliers, logistics providers, and equipment manufacturers, and will offer new opportunities for skilled workers.”

Analysts say the expansion comes as Russian steelmakers look to modernize facilities and enhance competitiveness. “There is a strategic push toward higher value-added products and more efficient production processes across the sector,” commented Elena Rybakova, metals analyst at the Russian Steel Industry Association. “Investments like this help position Russian producers for long-term growth, both domestically and in export markets, particularly in Eurasia and the Middle East.”

The project will incorporate advanced emissions control technologies, in line with Russia’s tightening environmental regulations. According to VolgoMetall, the new furnace will reduce specific energy consumption by around 12% compared to existing units, and the rolling mill will employ closed-loop water systems to minimize water usage.

VolgoMetall expects commissioning to begin in the third quarter of 2025, with full commercial operation targeted by year-end. “We are grateful for the support of regional authorities and our partners,” said Yermakov. “This investment will ensure that VolgoMetall remains a reliable supplier as our customers’ requirements evolve.”

The company said further details on technology providers and key contracts will be disclosed in the coming months.
